resolution.note: captured failed-unit systemctl/journal fixtures name failed + EADDRINUSE; captured locked /status fails doctor vault

title: Doctor and ship name a dead bw-serve unit and its journal reason instead of a bare unavailable
body:
Evidence 2026-11-17: bw-serve.service (transient systemd-run unit) failed at 15:28:42 with EADDRINUSE on ::1:8087 and stayed failed; every krn pr ship and lane ship then exited 70 with only "github-app-token: bw serve unavailable at http://localhost:8087" (lanes t-jfg2npc, t-dgkkmp1). Lanes reported it as a credential blocker without the cause. The remedy `bw-up` is correct (defined in ~/.config/krn/shell/bw.bash, interactive shells only); the operator ran it and doctor passed.
Outcome: when bw serve does not answer, doctor --unattended and the app-token error name the bw-serve unit state (failed / inactive / absent) and the last journal error line (e.g. EADDRINUSE), and say that `bw-up` is an operator command in an interactive shell.
Proof: a test with a captured `systemctl --user show bw-serve.service` and journal line for a failed unit asserts the message names "failed" and EADDRINUSE.
Files: src/cli/doctor-unattended.ts, src/ci/app-token.ts, test/cli/doctor-unattended.test.ts

Also (2026-11-17 17:5x): after the bw-serve unit was restarted with an empty BW_SESSION, GET localhost:8087/status reports "status":"locked" yet krn doctor --unattended prints PASS ("App token minted, vault session has 10.0h left"): the mint is served from the token cache and the vault check measures only the serve process age. Doctor must FAIL vault when /status is not unlocked; regression test with a captured locked /status body.
